info.title: Tack API
info.description: REST + WebSocket API for Tack, a lightweight, workflow-agnostic project-management tool. This contract is generated from the Rust handlers and domain models; it is the single source of truth for the wire format. All failing responses share the `{ "error": { "status", "message" } }` envelope.

get.summary: GET /api/backup — VACUUM INTO snapshot streamed as application/octet-stream.

post.summary:
POST /api/backup/remote — create a bundle and upload it to the configured S3
store. Bumps the sync generation and rejects with 409 when another device
has uploaded newer work, unless the request body carries `{"force": true}`.

requestBody.description: Optional `{ "force": true }` to override the newer-work guard

409.description: Not configured, or another device has newer work

post.summary: POST /api/backup/remote/restore — download a bundle and stage it for next restart.

409.description: Not configured, or restore would lose newer work

post.summary:
POST /api/backup/remote/verify — download a bundle and validate it (sha256 +
format + schema version) WITHOUT staging anything. Returns the manifest and
an `ok`/mismatch verdict so the UI can preview a restore safely.

`POST /api/items/{id}/dispatch` — enqueue a governed task on the item's
project's linked control plane. See the `dispatcher` module for the full
flow; this handler is just the HTTP boundary.
post.description:
**Trust default.** Unlike `dispatcher::dispatch_item`'s own required
`trusted: bool` parameter (no default, by design — see that module's
doc), this direct/manual entry point has no request body asking the
caller to state trust explicitly, so it resolves one via
`dispatcher::resolve_default_trust` — a conservative stopgap pending
card C2's `source: imported` marker (task 35.7). See that function's own
doc comment for exactly what it checks today and what it doesn't yet.

200.description: Dispatch outcome — branch on the `outcome` field, not HTTP status

404.description: Item not found, or orchestration disabled

409.description: Project not linked to a control plane, a dispatch for this item is already in flight, or the control plane could not be reached

`GET /api/metrics` — Prometheus text exposition merging Tack's own
work-tracking metrics (items by status, average cycle time, 7-day
throughput) with the latest mirrored sample of every metric docket has
reported for each linked control plane (task 34.7). One Grafana/Prometheus
scrape of this endpoint covers the whole factory.

200.description: Prometheus text exposition: Tack's own work-tracking metrics plus the latest mirrored docket sample per metric/label set

post.summary: POST /api/projects/from-template/:id - Create a project from a template

post.description:
Accepts the same snapshot shape produced by `export?format=json|yaml`. The
body is parsed as YAML when the `Content-Type` mentions YAML, otherwise JSON —
so a YAML export round-trips back in unchanged. (YAML is a JSON superset, so
both decode into the same intermediate `serde_json::Value`.)

requestBody.description: Project snapshot (JSON, or YAML when Content-Type mentions yaml) as produced by export

200.description: Import result with the new project and stats

get.summary:
`GET /api/projects/{id}/agent-activity` — one row per item in this project
that has at least one mirrored dispatch attempt, each carrying only its
latest attempt's raw status (the Board/List/Table badge's data source).
Does not 404 for an unknown `project_id` — mirrors `list_items`'s
precedent (`handlers/items.rs`) of just returning an empty result for a
project-scoped list rather than a bulk-fetch racing a project's own
lifecycle (e.g. deleted between the page loading and this poll).

200.description: Latest dispatch-attempt status per item with agent activity
Export file (JSON, YAML, or CSV per the `format` query)

post.description:
Accepts a UTF-8 CSV body (Content-Type: text/csv or text/plain).
First row must be column headers.  Only `title` is required; all other
columns are optional.  Recognised headers (case-insensitive):
  title, description, type, item_type, status, priority, assignee, estimate

Returns `{ "created": N, "skipped": N }`.

requestBody.description: CSV with a header row; `title` column required

200.description: Counts of created and skipped rows

post.description:
Fetches all (matching) issues from a GitHub repository and creates Tack
items for them.  Pull-request records are silently skipped.

Rate-limit note: unauthenticated calls are limited to 60 requests/hour by
GitHub; supplying a `token` raises this to 5 000 req/hour.

200.description: Counts of created/skipped issues and rate-limit remaining

400.description: Bad repo, token, or rate limit

post.description:
Fetches issues from Linear's GraphQL API and creates Tack items.
Pagination is cursor-based (50 issues per page).

200.description: Counts of created and skipped issues

400.description: Bad API key, filter, or rate limit

200.description: The project's control-plane link, if any

AgentBadgeResponse.description:
`GET /api/projects/{id}/agent-activity` response envelope — matches
`frontend/src/shared/agentActivity/api.ts`'s `AgentBadgeResponse` exactly
(`{ rows: [...] }`, not a bare array).

AgentBadgeRowResponse.description:
One row of `GET /api/projects/{id}/agent-activity` — the minimum a
Board/List/Table badge needs: an item's latest dispatch attempt's raw
status. See the module-level doc comment for the inner-join / tie-break
decisions.

ControlPlaneResponse.description:
Client-safe view of a `control_planes` row. Deliberately has **no** `token`
field — see the module doc.

health.description:
`"unknown"` | `"healthy"` | `"degraded"` | `"unreachable"` — driven by
the reconciler's health state machine (`tack-orch::reconciler`),
persisted verbatim.

token_set.description:
True when a docket Bearer token is currently stored for this plane.
The token itself is write-only over this API.

kind.description: Defaults to `"docket"` when omitted — the only kind implemented today.

token.description: docket Bearer token. Write-only: never echoed back in any response.

DispatchItemResponse.description:
`POST /api/items/{id}/dispatch` response. `outcome` is one of
`"dispatched"`, `"waiting_approval"`, `"already_in_flight"`,
`"no_dispatch_policy"`, `"not_eligible"`, `"blocked"` — every one of
these is a `200`, including `"blocked"`: docket gave a definitive,
well-formed refusal, which is a successful round-trip from Tack's HTTP
perspective, not a Tack-side error. Callers must branch on `outcome`,
not on HTTP status, to tell these apart. See `dispatcher::DispatchOutcome`
for the same taxonomy on the Rust side.

message.description:
Present only when `outcome == "blocked"` — docket's own message,
naming the guardrail policy id.

status_applied.description:
The Tack status `status_map` named for this trigger and actually
applied. Absent when `status_map` named no target for this trigger,
when the item was already there, or when the workflow engine
rejected it (see `status_map_rejected` below).

status_map_rejected.description:
Set when the workflow engine refused the `status_map`-driven
transition (TODO.md §0 rule 7 / task 35.6's `status_map_rejected`
outcome). The item was left exactly as it was; this is the engine's
own reason (e.g. an invalid transition or a WIP limit).

DispatchedTaskResponse.description:
A dispatched (or already-in-flight) `orch_tasks` row, projected for the
dispatch response. Deliberately smaller than `ItemAgentAttemptResponse`
(B6, `GET /items/{id}/agent-activity`) — no `run`/`events`/token-cost
fields, since a task this fresh has none of that mirrored yet.

status.description: HTTP status code, duplicated in the body for convenience.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
Structured error envelope returned by every failing endpoint — see
`crate::error::ApiError`. The body is always `{ "error": { status, message } }`.

FleetEntry.description:
One row per Tack project that has an `orch_links` row, joining: the link,
its control plane's reconciler-observed health, and mirrored cost/token/
approval data summed from `orch_tasks`/`orch_approvals`.

**Staleness must be representable.** `cost_usd_estimated` is `None`
whenever the plane is `unreachable` — never coerced to zero — so the UI can
grey the row and say "last seen Nm ago" instead of rendering a confident
zero (TODO.md §0 rule 6 / this card's acceptance bar). `Some(0.0)` means the
plane is reachable and genuinely has no mirrored cost yet. `tokens_in`/
`tokens_out` are always a plain (never-null) sum — per A5's contract, the
row component gates on `health`/`isStale()`, not per-field nullability, to
decide whether a number is trustworthy to render.

budget_usd.description: User-set cap, not a derived figure — deliberately unsuffixed.

cost_usd_estimated.description:
Estimated cumulative spend, summed from `orch_tasks` for this
project's items. `None` = plane unreachable, figure is stale/unknown.
`Some(0.0)` = plane reachable, nothing dispatched yet.

gateway.description:
`"active"` | `"inactive"` | `"unknown"`. **Always `"unknown"` in Wave
1** — `control_planes` has no persisted gateway column (see migration
019) and the reconciler only polls `/health` + `/status.json` for the
health state machine, not a stored gateway snapshot (card A2, 33.6). A
later wave that mirrors `FleetStatus.gateway` populates this for real.

last_activity_at.description:
Most recent `orch_tasks.dispatched_at` for this project's items, or
`None` if nothing has ever been dispatched. Real data (not a
placeholder) — computed from the same join as the cost/token sums —
but will always be `None` until Wave 3 (C1) starts dispatching.

pending_approval_count.description:
Pending docket approvals correlated to an item in this project (via
`orch_approvals.item_id`). Approvals with no item correlation surface
in the fleet-wide approvals inbox (Wave 4 / D1) instead of here.

pricing_snapshot_at.description:
Pricing-table snapshot date backing `cost_usd_estimated`. **Always
`None` in Wave 1** — no pricing-snapshot mechanism exists yet; a later
wave that adds one should populate this alongside real cost figures.

tokens_in.description:
Summed from `orch_tasks.tokens_in`/`tokens_out` for this project's
items. Real data, always `0` until Wave 3 dispatches anything — not a
placeholder, just an honest current total.

FleetListResponse.description:
`GET /api/fleet` response envelope — matches
`frontend/src/features/fleet/api.ts`'s `FleetResponse` exactly (`{ rows:
[...] }`, not a bare array).

FleetRosterMember.description:
One roster member — projected from a future live `FleetAgent` snapshot.
**Always an empty list in Wave 1**: no agent-roster table exists yet
(migrations 019–024 mirror control planes/links/tasks/runs/events/
approvals only). A later wave that adds roster mirroring populates this;
until then the field stays on the wire as `[]` rather than being removed,
so `frontend/src/features/fleet/api.ts`'s `FleetRow.roster` never needs a
shape change.

import_closed.description: Include closed issues (default: false — only open issues are imported).

label_filter.description:
When non-empty, only issues that carry at least one of these labels
are imported; all others are skipped.

repo.description: Repository as "owner/repo" or a full GitHub URL.

token.description:
Personal access token. Optional — unauthenticated calls are allowed
but are rate-limited to 60 requests/hour.

source.description:
Sticky provenance marker (Phase 35, card C2 — the prompt-injection
trust boundary): set once at creation time by whichever handler
created the item, and never mutated afterward — `UpdateItem` has no
`source` field, and the repository's `update_item` has no code path
that writes this column, so an item's source can never change once
set. `#[serde(default)]` matters here: any JSON that predates this
field (an old export, or a hand-built import payload) deserializes
to [`ItemSource::default()`] (`Unknown`), which [`ItemSource::is_trusted`]
treats as untrusted — the same "unverifiable provenance resolves to
untrusted" rule migration 029 applies to pre-existing database rows.

approvals.description: Newest-requested first; pending and decided both included.

attempts.description:
Newest attempt first (`orch_tasks.attempt DESC` — the repo layer's
`list_orch_tasks_for_item` already returns this order).

events_truncated.description:
See the module-level doc comment above `ItemAgentEventResponse` for
why this can't be a precise per-item fact and what it means instead.

ItemAgentApprovalResponse.description: One `orch_approvals` row for the item (pending or already decided).

ItemAgentAttemptResponse.description: One `orch_tasks` row (one dispatch attempt) for the item.

pricing_snapshot_at.description:
Always `null` — no pricing-snapshot mechanism exists anywhere in the
system yet (TODO.md §0 rule 6; same gap A4 found for the Fleet view's
identical field). Left `null` rather than invented.

ItemAgentRunResponse.description:
The `orch_runs` row correlated to an attempt via `remote_run_id`, if any
has been mirrored yet.

error.description:
Non-empty only when `state == "failed"`. Projected as an empty string,
never `null` — matches `ItemAgentRun.error: string` on the frontend
(deliberately not `string | null`, unlike `OrchRun.error` in the Rust
repo layer, which is `Option<String>`).

ItemDetail.description:
Detail envelope for `GET /api/items/{id}` — the item plus its assigned roles
and dependency edges.

ItemSource.description:
Where an item's title/description text came from. Backend for the
prompt-injection trust boundary (Phase 35, card C2): text imported from
GitHub Issues, Linear, or any bulk import is written by parties Tack
cannot vouch for, and becomes literal instructions to an autonomous
agent the moment the item is dispatched. [`is_trusted`](ItemSource::is_trusted)
is the single place that rule is encoded — nothing else in this codebase
should independently decide whether a `source` counts as trusted.

api_key.description: Linear personal API key (create at https://linear.app/settings/api).

import_completed.description: Include completed/cancelled issues (default: false — open only).

label_filter.description:
When non-empty, only issues carrying at least one matching label are
imported; all others are skipped.

project_id.description:
Import only issues belonging to this Linear project ID.  Overrides
`team_id` when both are set.

team_id.description:
Import only issues from this team (slug or ID). When omitted, all
issues accessible to the key are fetched.

OrchLinkResponse.description: Client-facing view of a project's control-plane link.

budget_usd.description:
User-set cap, not a derived spend figure — deliberately unsuffixed
(matches `orch_links.budget_usd`; TODO.md §0 rule 6).

OrchLinkView.description:
`GET /api/projects/{id}/orch-link` response. `linked: false` (with
`link: null`) is the ordinary state for a project that has never registered
a control plane — not an error, matching the `settings.rs` precedent for
optional per-scope config (no 404 for "not configured yet").

PaginatedItems.description:
Pagination envelope for the item-list endpoint (Phase 29.1). `total` is the
unpaginated match count so clients can render "N of M".

force.description: Override the "this device has newer work" guard.

key.description: Object key to restore. Defaults to the latest backup when omitted.

StatusMap.description:
`status_map` — TODO.md §1.3. All keys optional except `dispatch_from` (which
may be an empty list before a dispatch policy is configured — Wave 3 needs
it non-empty to actually dispatch, but registering a link ahead of that is
a normal, valid state in this wave). Every named status is validated against
the project's `WorkflowConfig` at save time — see [`validate_status_map`].
An absent key means "do not touch the item's status on that transition."

UpdateBackupSettings.description:
Incoming update. Any omitted/blank string field clears that override and
falls back to the environment default. A blank `secret_key` keeps the
existing stored secret (so the masked UI field can be left untouched).

retention.description:
Number of backups to keep. Must be at least 1 — `retention: 0` would
prune the backup that was just created (and, when it is the only one,
leave zero backups).

UpdateControlPlaneRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/control-planes/{id}` body. `token` is tri-state — see the module
doc and [`deserialize_some`]. `name`/`base_url` follow the ordinary
"absent means untouched" convention every other partial update in this API
uses.

token.description:
Absent = leave the stored token untouched. `null` = clear it. A string
= set/replace it.

WorkflowConfig.description: Full workflow configuration for a project.
